newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH FIRM PLANS WEB AUDIO CONFERENCE SYSTEM.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH FIRM PLANS WEB AUDIO CONFERENCE SYSTEM.

text.p: Finnish multimedia company A4 Media said on Friday it had developed what it believed was the first commercial service to transmit sound from media conferences live to the Internet.

"As far as we know this is the first service of its kind in the world," said managing director Markus Leikola. "The basic idea is that anyone who wants to hold a press conference can be assured of a live Internet audience by contracting with us."
The service, to be called Audioinfo, will launch at next week's summit between U.S. and Russian presidents Bill Clinton and Boris Yeltsin, Leikola said.
The Finnish foreign ministry has contracted A4 to provide live "streaming" audio, in English and Russian, of the presidents' planned press conference at web site www.summit.audioinfo.com, he said.

"Audioinfo offers a realistic alternative to complex and expensive telephone conference calls and will allow companies and other organisations to call a media conference at very short notice, far from a newspaper newsroom, and still be sure of coverage," he said.
The service requires relatively low-level end-user technology because it will not initially attempt to transmit video pictures, Leikola said.

"Anyone with a 14.4k modem and Real Audio software, which can be downloaded for free from the Internet, can connect," he said. "We have opted for a low bandwidth requirement to maximise the number of users."
All the audio files will be retained on the Web page for a fortnight after broadcast and A4 plans to offer the service internationally by the end of the year, Leikola said.
Subscribers will be charged an unspecified up-front fee to have a dedicated PC and software installed in their offices, and an additional sum for each media conference called.
A4 will post details of scheduled conferences on its Audioinfo web page www.finland.audioinfo.com.
